name: BEGGAR MY NEIGHBOUR
description: Beggar My Neighbour (also known as 'Strip Jack Naked') is a classic game of chance from the British 'War' family. Primarily played by children, it involves a 52-card deck distributed equally among players. The game is famous for its 'Payment' mechanic: when a face card is turned, the next player must pay a set number of cards. If another face card appears during payment, the obligation passes to the next player. It is a game of shifting fortunes where one can go from nearly winning the whole deck to being bankrupt in a few turns.

content.text: Beggar My Neighbour (also known as 'Strip Jack Naked') is a classic game of chance from the British 'War' family. Primarily played by children, it involves a 52-card deck distributed equally among players. The game is famous for its 'Payment' mechanic: when a face card is turned, the next player must pay a set number of cards. If another face card appears during payment, the obligation passes to the next player. It is a game of shifting fortunes where one can go from nearly winning the whole deck to being bankrupt in a few turns.

Originating in the United Kingdom in the early 19th century, it is one of the oldest recorded children's card games. It famously appears in Charles Dickens' 1861 novel 'Great Expectations', where the protagonist Pip plays it with Estella.
Deal the entire deck clockwise until all cards are distributed. Each player keeps their cards in a face-down pile (stack). No one may look at their cards.

items.text: Strip Jack Naked: An alternate name often used in Ireland and parts of the UK; rules are identical.
